challenges.name: safe-cache-keys-evidence
challenges.title: Safe cache keys: read the key and the headers
challenges.description: Two statements on the catalog cache incident: a data function whose key leaves out an input, and a public response whose result depends on a request header.

questions.explanation: False. The key leaves out inputs that change the result: level and locale are passed to db.listCourses, so the request for advanced courses at 09:14:05 is answered with the beginner list stored at 09:14:02. That is a correctness bug, not a hit-rate problem. "Public" only says the result does not depend on who asks; it still depends on every other input. The misconception mixes up the two failures of a key: a missing input gives wrong answers, an extra input (such as utm_source or the user id on public data) lowers the hit rate.

questions.question:
app/api/courses/route.ts:
const locale = request.headers.get("accept-language")?.slice(0, 2) ?? "en";
const courses = await getCourses(query, locale);   // titles are translated
return Response.json(courses, { headers: { "Cache-Control": "public, s-maxage=300" } });

Response headers of GET /api/courses?category=react (no Vary header):
cache-control: public, s-maxage=300
age: 41
x-cache: HIT

Statement: "For up to 300 seconds the CDN can serve the Vietnamese titles to a browser that sent Accept-Language: en, because the language changes the result but is neither in the URL nor named in a Vary header."
questions.explanation: True. A shared cache builds its key from the URL plus the request headers listed in Vary. Here the URL is the same for both languages and there is no Vary, so the first response stored (Vietnamese, if a Vietnamese browser asked first) is served to everyone for up to s-maxage=300 seconds. The fix is to make the locale part of the URL (/vi/api/courses) or to send Vary: Accept-Language and check your CDN supports it. The misconception is that the server cache key is the only key: every cache on the way builds its own.

challenges.name: safe-cache-keys
challenges.title: Build safe cache keys
challenges.description:
Every data request of app.codedev.test goes through cachePolicy(request), which returns the key of the server data cache (null = do not cache) and the Cache-Control header of the response. The old code cached the course list under "courses:<category>": advanced filters got the beginner list, Vietnamese learners got English titles and every newsletter link created a new entry. RESOURCES in the starter lists each resource with its classification (public, per-user, private-no-store), its route params, the query params the API understands with their defaults, whether it is localized, and sMaxAge.

Rules, in this order. (1) A resource that is not an own key of RESOURCES (for example "courses" or "toString") -> throw Error("unknown resource: <name>"). A route param of the resource that is missing or empty after trimming -> throw Error("missing param: <name>") for the first such param in RESOURCES order; extra params are ignored. Per-user or private-no-store data with a userId that is missing, null or empty after trimming -> throw Error("personal data needs a signed-in user").

(2) private-no-store -> { key: null, cacheControl: "private, no-store" }.

(3) The key is the resource name, then "/" + each route param value (trimmed) in RESOURCES order, then, only if the resource has query params, "?" + every known query param in alphabetical order as name=value joined by "&", then "|locale=<locale>" if the resource is localized, then "|user=<userId>" (trimmed) if it is per-user. A query value is the first one if the param is repeated (an array), trimmed and lower-cased; missing or empty means the default. Unknown query params are dropped. The locale is trimmed, lower-cased and cut at the first "-" ("vi-VN" -> "vi"); a language not in LOCALES, or no locale, becomes "en". Every param value, query value and user id put in the key goes through encodeURIComponent. Public keys never contain the user, even when one is signed in; non-localized keys never contain the locale.

(4) Cache-Control: public -> "public, max-age=0, s-maxage=<sMaxAge>", per-user -> "private, no-cache".

Input: { "requests": [{ resource, params?, query?, locale?, userId? }, ...] }. The runner prints "<key> | <cacheControl>" per request ("(not cached)" for a null key) or "error: <message>", then "<n> requests, <m> cache entries" (distinct keys).
hints: For each part of a request, ask: if only this part changed, would the API return a different result? If yes it belongs in the key, if no it must not be there. Which classification decides whether the user is such a part?

Look at the spec of the resource first: its query object gives you both the list of params to keep (its keys, to sort) and the value to use when one is missing or empty. Check the user rule before building anything, and remember that RESOURCES["toString"] is not undefined on a plain object.

A similar key for a different resource: a forum thread list with query defaults { order: "latest", page: "1" }, not localized, public. The request ?page=2&order=&ref=mail normalizes to order=latest (empty -> default) and page=2, ref is dropped, giving "threads?order=latest&page=2"; the same thread list for a signed-in user gives the same key, because the list does not depend on who reads it.
